speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Can you describe the bleeding from your wisdom tooth extraction in terms of duration and severity, and have you noticed any unusual bruising elsewhere on your body?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient was brought in by his mother for persistent bleeding following elective removal of wisdom teeth. The bleeding from the surrounding gums was minimally responsive to multiple gauze packs. The patient also has a history of easy bruising. Family history includes the patient's uncle who had similar issues with bleeding and a history of easy bruising and joint swelling.

speaker: Doctor
text: Has the patient experienced any joint bleeding or swelling, particularly in the knees or elbows, and does his family history suggest an X-linked pattern with affected males on his mother's side?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Persistent bleeding from gums following tooth extraction. I also have History of easy bruising, Family history of similar bleeding problems and joint swelling.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does the patient have a personal history of bleeding into his own joints, and has he experienced excessive bleeding from other minor cuts or previous dental procedures? I would like to check his coagulation profile, so REQUEST TEST: PT, PTT, and Factor VIII and IX levels.

speaker: Doctor
text: The prolonged PTT with normal platelet count and bleeding time suggests a factor deficiency rather than a platelet disorder. Given the family history and your symptoms, I need to distinguish between Hemophilia A and B, so I will review the specific factor levels from the previous request. REQUEST TEST: Factor VIII and IX levels.

speaker: Doctor
text: Since Factor VIII and IX levels are normal, we must look for other causes of isolated prolonged PTT, such as a factor XI deficiency or an inhibitor like lupus anticoagulant. REQUEST TEST: Factor XI level and Lupus Anticoagulant test.

speaker: Doctor
text: With normal Factor VIII, IX, and XI levels, I suspect a deficiency in the contact activation factors, such as Factor XII, prekallikrein, or high-molecular-weight kininogen. REQUEST TEST: Factor XII, Prekallikrein, and High-Molecular-Weight Kininogen levels.

speaker: Doctor
text: With all coagulation factors and contact activation proteins normal, I must rule out platelet function disorders that can present with bleeding despite normal counts. REQUEST TEST: Platelet Aggregation Studies.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the normal coagulation profile and platelet function studies, I suspect von Willebrand Disease, which can sometimes present with normal or mildly prolonged PTT and normal platelet counts. REQUEST TEST: Von Willebrand Factor Antigen and Ristocetin Cofactor Activity.

speaker: Doctor
text: With all standard coagulation and platelet function tests normal, I need to assess for a rare factor deficiency like Factor XIII, which does not affect PT or PTT. REQUEST TEST: Factor XIII activity level.
